schemes.official_name: Learning Factory Capstone Design (College of Engineering senior capstone)
schemes.module_code: Departmental capstone design courses (codes vary by department)
schemes.description: Senior-year engineering capstone supported by the Learning Factory: teams of 4-6 students design a product, process, software or service for a sponsoring client (companies, government offices, some Penn State units). Teams write a Statement of Work and Detailed Specification Report that are reviewed with the instructor and submitted to the sponsor, build alpha prototypes (weeks 11-12), and finish with a final report, poster and summary plus the Design Showcase in weeks 14-15.
schemes.eligible_faculties_programmes: College of Engineering senior students in departments using Learning Factory capstone (e.g. EECS, aerospace, ESM, mechanical, biological engineering pages cite Learning Factory sponsorship)
schemes.eligibility_restrictions: Engineering capstone students; programme page says capstone programs 'may differ slightly by department'
schemes.credit_assessment: Credit and compulsory status not stated on pages fetched (supports 'the capstone engineering design course'; requirements follow the individual degree).
schemes.delivery_format: Team design project with sponsor; in-class meetings; Design Showcase
schemes.project_evidence: Defined sponsor project with Statement of Work, specification report, alpha prototype, final report, poster and Design Showcase [1][2].
schemes.group_evidence: Teams form in week 1 ('Show up to class and meet teammates') [2]; fall 2025 showcase: teams of four to six students [3].
schemes.employer_evidence: Projects are 'sponsored by clients' [1]; teams submit Statement of Work and Detailed Specification Report to the sponsor and meet the sponsor at kickoff [2]; sponsors pay a $4,000 fee for a Senior Capstone Design project [4]; fall 2025 showcase judged by industry experts and past sponsors, winners sponsored by e.g. Northrop Grumman, Seco Tools, Walmart Inc., Aluminum Association, Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren [3].
schemes.partner_role: Client/sponsor: supplies project, pays fee, receives specification documents and showcase results. Mostly external companies and government offices; at least one of 13 fall 2025 winning projects was sponsored by a Penn State unit (Center for Immersive Learning and Digital Innovation) [3], so a small internal share exists.
schemes.named_partners: Fall 2025 showcase winners: Northrop Grumman, Seco Tools, Walmart Inc., Aluminum Association Inc., Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division, Fleet Equipment Corporation, Hungry Group [3]
schemes.deliverable: Prototype, final report, poster, summary, Design Showcase presentation; Statement of Work and specification report to sponsor
schemes.participation_data: Fall 2025 winning projects only: 13 projects / 63 students (winners tally from news article; total participation not published in sources fetched).
schemes.unresolved: Whether capstone is compulsory in every engineering degree; total number of teams/sponsors per year; which departments run capstone outside the Learning Factory.

profile_md: Penn State's verified employer-linked group project provision is college-based rather than university-wide. The strongest route is the College of Engineering senior capstone supported by the Learning Factory: teams of 4-6 deliver a Statement of Work, specification report, prototype, final report and showcase for a sponsor who pays $4,000; the fall 2025 showcase (11 Dec 2025) shows current delivery with company and government sponsors (Northrop Grumman, Walmart, NSWC Dahlgren), though a small share of sponsors are Penn State units. Whether the capstone is compulsory varies by department. In Smeal, the Nittany Lion Consulting Group and capstone consulting teams (MBA and Sapphire honors students) work with business and non-profit clients, but the page could not be opened and named clients date from 2020-21, so current delivery is unclear. IST 440W is a team capstone with some external clients (Brandywine 2021 example). CommAgency (Bellisario) is a competitive student agency whose documented clients are University units, so it fails the external-organisation test. No qualifying route was verified in Science, Liberal Arts or Law/Arts & Architecture. Further departmental capstones likely exist.
gaps: Smeal page (503) not read; current NLCG/Smeal capstone status; IST 440W current client practice; compulsory status of Learning Factory capstone by department; other engineering departmental capstones, COMM 473, Career Accelerator pilot; Eberly College of Science only one query.
